title: Rules, rights and duties at school

pedagogy.rationale: Teacher-led, oral and picture-supported short scenes for emergent readers, with choices read aloud and performance shown by role-play.

prerequisiteAssumptions: Can listen to a short spoken story and answer who and what questions about it.
Knows familiar places such as home, school and market by name.

misconceptions.description: Thinks rules exist only so adults can punish children.
misconceptions.response: Rules help everyone stay safe and be treated fairly. Ask: who does this rule keep safe?

misconceptions.description: Thinks a rule only matters when an adult is watching.
misconceptions.response: The road is just as dangerous when no one is looking. We follow rules to keep people safe, not to avoid being seen.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a right is anything a child wants, such as sweets every day.
misconceptions.response: A right is something every child needs and should have, like being safe and going to school.
Children have duties too: listening when others speak and keeping the classroom clean.

scenes.title: The ball and the road
scenes.learnerAction: Listen to the story and look at the picture.

content.body:
Musu and Kollie both want the ball. They push each other. The ball rolls toward the road.

What should they do? Today we learn about **rules**, **rights** and **duties**.

media.description: Two children at a school gate; a ball rolls toward a road.
media.altText: Two children push each other at the school gate while their ball rolls toward the road.

accessibility.textAlternative: A short story: two children push over a ball, and the ball rolls toward the road.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue to move to the next scene.

offline.note: The teacher can tell the story without the picture.

content.body:
Today we will:

1. Name a rule and say how it keeps us safe or fair.
2. Tell a right from a duty.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two goals: naming a rule and why it helps, and telling a right from a duty.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue to move to the next scene.

offline.note: The teacher reads the goals aloud.

scenes.title: Listen and answer
scenes.learnerAction: Listen to your teacher and choose an answer.

content.body: Your teacher reads: *Fatu walked to the market with her mother. They bought rice.*

options.feedback: Yes! Fatu went with her mother.
Listen again: Fatu went with her mother.

items.prompt: Where do children go to learn to read?

options.feedback: We buy food at the market. We learn to read at school.
Yes! We learn to read at school.

accessibility.textAlternative: A two-sentence story about Fatu and two spoken questions with two answers each.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to an answer and press Space.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: The teacher reads the choices aloud and the child points or says the answer.

offline.note: The teacher can ask the questions aloud.

scenes.title: Why we have rules
scenes.learnerAction: Listen and repeat the two reasons.

content.body:
A **rule** tells us what to do or not do.

Rules help in two ways:

- They keep us **safe**.
- They help us be **fair**.
keyPoints: Walk near the road: it keeps us safe.
Take turns with the ball: it is fair.

media.description: A child walking beside a road; two children taking turns with a ball.
media.altText: Left: a child walking safely beside the road. Right: two children taking turns with a ball.

accessibility.textAlternative: A rule tells us what to do. Rules keep us safe and help us be fair, with two examples.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue to move to the next scene.

offline.note: The teacher can act out both examples.

scenes.title: Let's think it through
scenes.learnerAction: Tap to see each step of the story.

content.body: Back to Musu, Kollie and the ball. Tap to see what a rule can do.

steps.label: The problem
steps.description: They push, and the ball rolls to the road.

steps.label: Safe rule
steps.description: Do not run into the road. Ask a grown-up to get the ball.

steps.label: Fair rule
steps.description: Take turns. Musu kicks first, then Kollie.

steps.label: Why
steps.description: Now nobody gets hurt, and both children play.

accessibility.textAlternative: Four steps: the problem, a safety rule, a fairness rule, and why the rules help.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Press Enter to see each step, then Continue.

offline.note: The teacher can tell each step aloud.

scenes.title: Rights and duties
scenes.learnerAction: Listen and say each word with your teacher.

content.body:
A **right** is something every child should have.
Every child has a right to be safe and to go to school.

A **duty** is something we should do.
At school our duties are to listen and to keep the classroom clean.

accessibility.textAlternative: A right is something every child should have, like being safe. A duty is something we should do, like listening.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue to move to the next scene.

scenes.title: Right or duty?
scenes.learnerAction: Listen and choose right or duty.

content.body: Remember: a right is what you **should have**. A duty is what you **should do**.

items.prompt: Going to school. Right or duty?

options.feedback: Yes! Every child should have school.
School is something every child should have. That makes it a right.

items.prompt: Picking up your rubbish. Right or duty?

options.feedback: Picking up rubbish is something we should do. That makes it a duty.
Yes! It is something we should do.

hints: Ask: should I have it, or should I do it?

accessibility.textAlternative: Two read-aloud questions: is going to school, or picking up rubbish, a right or a duty?
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to an answer and press Space.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Children stand for a right and sit for a duty while the teacher reads.

offline.note: Can be played as stand-or-sit without a device.

items.prompt: Kollie walks near the road only when the teacher is looking. Is that good?

options.feedback: The road is dangerous even when nobody is looking. The rule keeps Kollie safe all the time.
Right! The rule keeps him safe all the time, not only when someone is watching.

items.prompt: Musu says, 'Sweets every day is my right.' Is it?

options.feedback: Sweets are nice, but a right is something every child needs, like being safe.
Right! Sweets are a want. Being safe and going to school are rights.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two read-aloud yes-or-no questions about following a rule when nobody watches, and whether sweets are a right.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to an answer and press Space.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Children show thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no.

offline.note: Can be asked aloud without a device.

scenes.title: Your turn
scenes.learnerAction: Choose on your own. No help this time.

content.body: Your turn. Choose on your own.

items.prompt: 'Wash your hands before you eat.' Why do we have this rule?

options.text: To keep us healthy and safe
options.feedback: Yes! Clean hands help stop sickness.

options.text: So the teacher can punish us
options.feedback: Rules help us. This one keeps us healthy.

items.prompt: Listening when a friend is talking. Right or duty?

options.feedback: Listening is something we should do. That is a duty.
Yes! It is something we should do.

items.prompt: Being safe at school. Right or duty?

options.feedback: Yes! Every child should be safe.
Being safe is something every child should have. That is a right.

accessibility.textAlternative: Three read-aloud questions: why we wash hands, and whether listening and being safe are rights or duties.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to an answer and press Space.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: The teacher reads the choices and the child says or points to an answer.

offline.note: Questions and feedback are saved with the lesson.

scenes.title: Tell your teacher
scenes.learnerAction: Say your answers. Your teacher writes them down.

content.body: Say your answers. Your teacher can write them for you.

prompts.prompt: Tell one rule at home or school, and how it helps.
Tell one duty you have at school.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two spoken prompts: tell a rule and how it helps, and tell a duty at school.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab into each box; the teacher types what the child says.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Children answer aloud and the teacher records the answers.

offline.note: Answers are spoken; the teacher can write them on paper.

scenes.title: Show what you know
scenes.learnerAction: Show your teacher on your own.

content.body: Your teacher will ask you to act out and tell. Do it on your own. Your teacher checks it, not this lesson.

fallback.content: Your teacher asks you to act out a rule and to tell a right and a duty, then writes down what you show.

accessibility.textAlternative: The teacher asks each child to act out a rule and tell a right and a duty.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue when the teacher says you are done.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Done in person with the teacher; no device needed.

offline.note: The teacher runs this in person and records each child's response.

scenes.title: Back to Musu and Kollie
scenes.learnerAction: Tell a partner what Musu and Kollie should do.

content.body:
What should Musu and Kollie do about the ball? Tell a partner.

Next week your teacher will ask about rules, rights and duties again.

accessibility.textAlternative: Tell a partner what the children should do about the ball; the topic returns next week.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Use Continue to finish the lesson.
